topPRs.title: kona-node,op-devstack!: add a consensus-layer sync mode that derives without gossip
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #24345 (base `joshklop/kona-engine-derivation-channel`), so the diff shows only this change. Stack, in merge order: #23883 → #23859 → #24339 → #24344 → #24345 → **this PR**.

A kona-node validator does not derive anything from L1 until an unsafe payload from gossip makes the execution layer answer a forkchoice update with `VALID`. A validator with no peers, behind a halted sequencer, or restarted with p2p disconnected never derives, so it cannot follow the safe chain or L1-forced deposits. op-node derives from L1 in that situation, because its default is `--syncmode=consensus-layer`.

kona-node now takes `--syncmode` with op-node's two values. `execution-layer` is the default, so existing nodes do not change. With `consensus-layer`, a validator resets its engine at startup, as a sequencer already does, and starts deriving from L1 if the execution layer answers that forkchoice update with `VALID`.

Two limits a reviewer should know about:
- **It is not op-node's full consensus-layer sync.** An unsafe payload with a gap before it still makes the execution layer sync, and no queue holds such payloads until derivation fills the gap. That is ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#574, and ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#631 stays open for it.
- **`SYNCING` at startup falls back to today's behaviour.** The validator then waits for an unsafe payload and logs a warning. The reset is not retried, because a pending reset holds back the queued unsafe payloads that drive EL sync. `--syncmode.offset-el-safe` does not apply to the startup reset.

A heuristic cannot replace the flag: an isolated fresh verifier and a new node that should wait for EL sync both start with an execution layer at genesis and no gossip.

op-devstack now passes each kona-node its role's sync mode; it used to ignore it. Devstack's default is CL sync, so nearly every kona-node verifier in the acceptance suite now runs in `consensus-layer` mode, like op-node. That lets `TestSDMPostExecBlockDerivesOnIsolatedVerifier` and `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterSafeReorg` run on kona-node. Both keep their verifier off p2p and expect it to derive from L1; both fail when kona-node is forced back to `execution-layer`.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22271
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22275

Reviewed with the `rust-code-reviewer`, `go-code-reviewer` and `safedb-reviewer` agents; `safedb-reviewer` had no findings. Not done:
- Locally, on kona-node, I ran the `base/conductor`, `base/chain`, `base/deposit`, `sync`, `sdm`, `derivation`, `safedb_parity`, `safeheaddb_clsync`, `safeheaddb_elsync`, `depreqres`, `sync_tester`, `sequencer` and `batcher` packages. The interop, proofs and supernode packages are left to CI; `safedb_proof_consumers` needs a cannon prestate I did not build.
- No test checks the safe head database contents across the startup reset.

**Findings dismissed, for the author to confirm:**
- *Make `EngineActor::with_startup_reset` `pub(crate)`.* Kept public, because `EngineActor::new` is public and a caller that builds the actor itself needs it.
- *The re-peer calls in `safedb_parity` and `derivation/restart` may no longer be needed on kona-node.* Left in place; only their comments changed, to stop saying kona-node needs gossip to resume deriving.

BREAKING CHANGE: affects code that builds a kona node through kona-node-service, and tests that run kona-node in op-devstack. `RollupNodeBuilder` has a new public field `sync_mode`, so code that builds it with a struct literal must set it; `RollupNodeBuilder::new` callers are unaffected and can call `with_sync_mode`. In op-devstack, a kona-node now honours `SequencerSyncMode` and `VerifierSyncMode`: a verifier with the default CL sync resets its engine at startup and derives from L1 without waiting for gossip. A test that relied on a kona-node verifier waiting for gossip must set `VerifierSyncMode` to EL sync.
